theory: the real-body slice with the cached 2s boot can carry a stranger's first minute without any engine edit: first-run on-page guidance in plain words, every control named on the page and keyboard-first (the mouse-through-automation unreliability law), boot->motion->understood-control->deliberate-action->restart each timed, a clean restart, and zero console errors -- measured by a private headless-browser walkthrough acting as the stranger
prereg: record.md (this directory), committed before any code (governing: 4ff5576e; duplicate dispatch reconciled: DUPLICATE_ASSIGNMENT.md)

instrument.how: a private headless Playwright browser (fresh context, never the shared desktop) opens the page, reads ONLY what the page itself shows, and acts: it names the first control from the page's own objective text, presses every key the page names and verifies each by its stage effect, restarts with R, and captures console+pageerror+requestfailed for the whole session plus the on-page error beacon
instrument.channel_law: the prereg names channel 'chrome': the instrument ATTEMPTS it every run via a navigation canary; the machine's installed Chrome fails it (FINDING F-ENV-CHROME below), so the run completes on Playwright's bundled Chromium of the same build and the deviation is recorded verbatim in every artifact
instrument.hardening: per-stage trace lines, 10 s budget on every page.evaluate, 5 s on every press, a 240 s session watchdog, kill-safe browser close, and progressive artifact flush -- a wedged call can no longer cost the run its artifact (the run-6 lesson)

findings.detail: the machine's installed Chrome 153.0.8010.53 hangs EVERY real navigation: loopback and external, headless and full binary, inside Playwright and via chrome --dump-dom directly; instant pre-connect rejections still work; the netlog shows the request sent and no response headers ever (netlog_probe.json, probe_*.js all committed). It broke mid-session between early walkthrough runs. The instrument therefore canaries channel chrome every run and completes on the same build's bundled Chromium when the canary fails -- all three receipt runs record this deviation verbatim

findings.class: product defect caught by the falsifier
findings.detail: the key handler matched k.key (undefined on every KEYLIST entry) instead of k.name, so NO named key had a working path in any earlier run -- the page looked alive but every key was dead. Exactly the defect F-EVERY-NAMED-KEY exists to catch; fixed, and the honest RED artifacts kept

findings.class: measurement bug fixed in the instrument's target
findings.detail: boot_count was derived from an events list that RESETS on every boot, so a real restart could never increment it (measured boots [1,1] twice). The server now carries a cumulative counter; the walkthrough verifies it harness-side

the page's original pollers had no in-flight guard or timeout: under machine load the 9 MB /api/verts fetches stacked by the thousands (ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES, 4233 errors in run 1) and the server queue collapsed. Fixed: serialized polling + AbortSignal.timeout on the three polling endpoints; by-design aborts counted separately from errors
